matches.quote: They acknowledge that the data rise below H*, contrary to the model. It is therefore not shown that the kink uniquely signals a finite Δmin
The peak position and height also depend on the chosen Γ/Δ0 = 0.002 and c = 0.15... The absence of a peak in the data therefore cannot discriminate
no error bars are shown in Fig. 4b,c. The 'kink' could thus be within the systematic uncertainty of the extrapolation.
the abstract claim that the T-dependence is 'consistent with a small superconducting gap' is never tested quantitatively... no fit or overlay with the pseudo-node calculation is shown.
In a superconductor, however, κph can be field dependent: field-induced quasiparticles and vortices scatter phonons.
In the pseudo-node model, H∥c is also perpendicular to the b-axis minima and to jQ. It should therefore display its own threshold
In UTe2 the measured Hc2, particularly along b, is strongly affected by non-orbital physics... Whether the curves look 'isotropic' below H* therefore depends on this normalization choice.
The text reports κb/T ∝ T² at low T, i.e. κ ∝ T³. This is also the canonical boundary-limited phonon form.

notes: C4 and C5 rely on Supplementary Fig. S2 (not included in the main text), so the review could not inspect the 6 T Wiedemann-Franz curve directly. C7 and C12 are marked 'partly' because the review raises closely related criticisms (lack of quantitative theory-data comparison for zero-field κ/T(T) and whether a nodal model explains the low-field κ0(H) rise/kink) without framing them in the exact terms of Δ0/Tc or the Fig. 4c subtraction masking the low-field rise.
